To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

barrier-island deposits can be identified by the following characteristics: (1) a relatively thin, discontinuous veneer of sand over a thick, discontinuous, fine-grained, organic-rich deposit; (2) a thin, discontinuous, sandy deposit over a thick, continuous, fine-grained deposit; or (3) a thick, continuous sand deposit with a thin, discontinous, organic-rich layer.
the sedimentation of barrier islands is influenced by island migration.

Barrier-island deposits are characterized by: a) a wide range of grain size and sorting, b) an abundance of fine sand to very fine sand (medium to fine sand is rare), c) an abundance of shell debris and shell fragments, d) a lack of coarse sand and pebbles, and e) a lack of heavy minerals.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the characteristics of barrier islands and the sedimentary deposits associated with them; (2) the processes of sedimentation that occur in barrier-island environments and the influence of these processes on sedimentary deposits; (3) the influence of barrier migration on the sedimentation of barrier islands and associated environments; and (4) the influence of erosion on barrier-island deposits and the subsequent interpretation of the sediments.
the influence of channel migration on the sedimentary characteristics of barrier deposits.
the sedimentation of the barrier-islands of the Gulf of Mexico and the effects of island migration on barrier-island deposits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
barrier-island sediments are the result of the interaction of the barrier-islet environment with other environments.
barrier islands do not migrate along the coasts of Texas and Louisiana.
the migration of a barrier island along a coast is an extremely important process in the development of the sedimentation pattern and the sediment characteristics of a coastal area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a major part of the barrier deposits are reworked from other environments.
the barrier-island depositional environment has been modified by island migration.
the barrier-island deposits are not a distinct sedimentary unit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
barrier-island deposits are not always easily recognized.
the barrier island deposits can be used as a proxy for the paleo-environment of the adjacent channel, which is a very useful tool for paleo-environmental reconstruction.
